correctness.rationale: The proof derives strict positive projections at diametral corners from the Euclidean diameter inequality, localizes all near-maximum pairs to finitely many cone pairs, proves independent corner Poisson limits for n^(1/2) local sample points, and uses uniform Taylor bounds to establish the minimum-of-sums weak limit. Cone triangle area and void probabilities yield correct marginal and joint rates; positive intersection yields strict covariance. Four-dimensional simplex integration and finite inclusion-exclusion yield t^4/6 and epsilon^4/3 constants, with higher-order remainders. The standalone script checked equilateral, isosceles and rectangular geometric constants. Finite tests are supplemental only.

value.rationale: The problem of maximum sample interpoint distance on regular even polygons had known decoupled limits but the essential disjoint-endpoint restriction is broken by ordinary nonregular triangles. The theorem identifies all possible vertex-graph dependencies for every convex polygon, proves a sharp independence criterion and supplies a universal rare-event coefficient; it yields an explicit nonregular dependent two-diameter example. This is a structural classification useful for extreme-value asymptotics rather than a minor table extension.
